decisions.choice: the command promised in 25:16-18 is now carried out
decisions.reason: After the sin at Peor the LORD had told Moses to treat the Midianites as enemies, because they had led Israel astray there and in the affair of Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite leader (25:16-18). This chapter tells how that order was carried out.

en.R: "Punish the Midianites for what they did to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. After that you will die and join your ancestors."

ko.L: "이스라엘 자손의 원수를 미디안 사람들에게 갚아라. 그 후에 너는 네 백성들에게로 모여 갈 것이다."
ko.B: "이스라엘 백성을 위하여 미디안 사람들에게 원수를 갚아라. 그 뒤에 너는 조상들에게로 돌아갈 것이다."
ko.R: "미디안 사람들이 이스라엘 사람들에게 한 일에 대하여 그들을 벌하여라. 그 일을 마친 뒤에 너는 죽어서 조상들 곁으로 갈 것이다."

pt.L: "Vinga a vingança dos filhos de Israel contra os midianitas; depois serás reunido aos teus povos."
pt.B: "Executa a vingança dos israelitas contra os midianitas. Depois disso serás reunido ao teu povo."
pt.R: "Castiga os midianitas pelo que fizeram aos israelitas. Depois disso morrerás e irás para junto dos teus antepassados."

decisions.choice: avenge the vengeance: bring just punishment for a wrong done
decisions.reason: The verb and its noun are the language of paying back a wrong, here the harm Midian did by drawing Israel into idolatry and the plague that followed (25:1-9, 17-18). In the next verse the same punishment is called "the vengeance of the LORD" (verse 3): the wrong was done against the LORD as well as against Israel.

decisions.choice: gathered to your peoples: you will die
decisions.reason: This is the regular way of speaking of a death that joins a person to his ancestors (Genesis 25:8; Numbers 20:24, 26). The LORD had already told Moses that he would die after seeing the land (27:12-13). The Hebrew word is plural, "peoples", meaning his kin.

decisions.choice: punish ... for what they did to / die and join your ancestors
decisions.reason: Readable says what "avenge the vengeance" is about and spells out the idiom of being gathered to one's people.

decisions.choice: Venge la vengeance
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew pairing of verb and noun from the same root, as the English Literal does; Balanced says "tire vengeance des Madianites", the ordinary French phrase.

decisions.choice: "báo thù"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads it as just punishment for a wrong; "báo thù" is the more formal word used for the LORD's vengeance, where "trả thù" sounds like personal spite.

decisions.choice: "원수를 갚다" (Literal, Balanced), "벌하다" (Readable) for "avenge the vengeance"
decisions.reason: The phrase is bringing just punishment for a wrong done (meaning decision); "원수를 갚다" keeps the Hebrew's picture of righting a wrong, and Readable says plainly that it is punishment, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Midiã (the land and the people as a whole), os midianitas (the people), Fineias, Eleazar, Balaão, filho de Beor
decisions.reason: For the chapter, the names as the Portuguese of Numbers uses them: "Midiã" and "os midianitas", as Genesis and Exodus have it, "Fineias" (1990 spelling) and "Balaão", the usual Brazilian forms. "Madiã" is the older Catholic form.

decisions.choice: Vinga a vingança (L); Executa a vingança (B); Castiga (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew doubling of verb and noun (m1), which Portuguese can say; Balanced says "executar a vingança", the phrase for carrying out a just retribution, and Readable "castigar", as the English "punish".

vi.L: Và Môi-se nói với dân chúng rằng: "Hãy trang bị vũ khí cho những người trong các ngươi đi ra trận, và để họ đi đánh Ma-đi-an, để thực hiện sự báo thù của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} trên Ma-đi-an.

ko.B: 그래서 모세가 백성에게 말했다. "너희 가운데서 사람들을 무장시켜 전쟁에 나가게 하여라. 그들이 미디안을 쳐서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 원수를 미디안에게 갚게 하여라.

pt.L: E Moisés falou ao povo, dizendo: "Armem dentre vocês homens para o exército, e que eles vão contra Midiã para executar a vingança {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} contra Midiã.

decisions.choice: the vengeance of the LORD: the same punishment the LORD called Israel's vengeance in verse 2
decisions.reason: The LORD spoke of avenging Israel; Moses speaks of the LORD's vengeance. Both are true of one act: the war is not a private feud but a judgment the LORD orders on a people who had led Israel into sin against him (25:17-18).

decisions.choice: arm: equip and prepare men for battle
decisions.reason: The verb is used of men made ready and armed for war (32:20-21; Joshua 4:13). Verse 5 calls the chosen men "armed for war" with the same root.

decisions.choice: let them go against Midian
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "let them be against Midian", a way of saying that they will attack it. English needs a verb of movement.

decisions.choice: a thousand to the tribe, a thousand to the tribe: a thousand from each tribe
decisions.reason: Saying the phrase twice is the Hebrew way of saying "each" (as in 13:2, "one man, one man for each tribe"). Every tribe sends the same number, so all Israel shares in the war, though only a small force goes. On the word "thousand", see the note at 1:21.

decisions.choice: were provided: were handed over or made available for service
decisions.reason: The verb is rare. It seems to mean to hand over or set apart, so the men were supplied by their tribes for this war. Some take it as "were counted off"; the sense is much the same.

decisions.choice: the thousands of Israel: the clans of Israel
decisions.reason: Here "thousands" names the large family units of the tribes, as in 1:16, while the second "thousand" in the verse is the number. The total, 12,000, is simply a thousand for each of the twelve tribes.

decisions.choice: the clans of Israel
decisions.reason: As in 1:16, Balanced and Readable say "clans" for the units, so that the reader does not take them for numbers. Literal keeps "thousands".

decisions.choice: "các dòng họ" for "the thousands of Israel"
decisions.reason: As Numbers 1:16 in Vietnamese: the "thousands" are the clans.

decisions.choice: "이스라엘의 천천" (Literal), "이스라엘의 여러 가문" (Balanced, Readable) for "the thousands of Israel"
decisions.reason: The thousands here are the clans of Israel (meaning decision); Literal keeps the Hebrew word in "천천" ("thousands upon thousands" in older Korean), Balanced and Readable name the clans.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח אֹתָ֥ם מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶ֥לֶף לַמַּטֶּ֖ה לַצָּבָ֑א אֹ֠תָם וְאֶת־פִּ֨ינְחָ֜ס בֶּן־אֶלְעָזָ֤ר הַכֹּהֵן֙ לַצָּבָ֔א וּכְלֵ֥י הַקֹּ֛דֶשׁ וַחֲצֹצְר֥וֹת הַתְּרוּעָ֖ה בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent them Moses, a thousand to [the] tribe, to the army, them and Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to the army, and [the] vessels of the holy [place] and [the] trumpets of the alarm [were] in his hand.

en.L: And Moses sent them, a thousand from each tribe, to the war, them and Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, to the war, and the holy articles and the trumpets for the alarm [were] in his hand.
en.B: Moses sent them to the war, a thousand from each tribe, together with Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, who had in his care the holy articles and the trumpets for sounding the alarm.
en.R: Moses sent them to war, a thousand men from each tribe. He also sent Phinehas, the son of Eleazar the priest. Phinehas took with him the holy objects and the trumpets for sounding the alarm.

es.L: Y Moisés los envió, mil por tribu, a la guerra, a ellos y a Finés hijo de Eleazar el sacerdote, a la guerra, y los objetos santos y las trompetas de la alarma [estaban] en su mano.
es.B: Moisés los envió a la guerra, mil por tribu, junto con Finés hijo de Eleazar el sacerdote, que tenía a su cargo los objetos santos y las trompetas para tocar la alarma.
es.R: Moisés los envió a la guerra, mil hombres de cada tribu. También envió a Finés, el hijo de Eleazar el sacerdote. Finés llevó consigo los objetos santos y las trompetas para tocar la alarma.

fr.L: Et Moïse les envoya, mille par tribu, à la guerre, eux et Phinéas fils d’Éléazar le prêtre, à la guerre, et les objets saints et les trompettes de l’alarme [étaient] dans sa main.
fr.B: Moïse les envoya à la guerre, mille par tribu, avec Phinéas fils d’Éléazar le prêtre, qui avait sous sa garde les objets saints et les trompettes pour sonner l’alarme.
fr.R: Moïse les a envoyés à la guerre, mille hommes de chaque tribu. Il a aussi envoyé Phinéas, le fils d’Éléazar le prêtre. Phinéas a emporté avec lui les objets saints et les trompettes pour sonner l’alarme.

sw.L: Musa akawatuma, elfu moja kwa kabila, vitani, wao na Finehasi mwana wa Eleazari kuhani, vitani, na vyombo vitakatifu na tarumbeta za kupiga hatari [vilikuwa] mkononi mwake.
sw.B: Musa aliwatuma vitani, elfu moja kutoka kila kabila, pamoja na Finehasi mwana wa Eleazari kuhani, aliyekuwa na vyombo vitakatifu na tarumbeta za kupiga ishara ya hatari chini ya uangalizi wake.
sw.R: Musa aliwatuma vitani wanaume elfu moja kutoka kila kabila. Pia alimtuma Finehasi, mwana wa Eleazari kuhani. Finehasi alichukua pamoja naye vitu vitakatifu na tarumbeta za kupiga ishara ya hatari.

vi.L: Và Môi-se sai họ, một nghìn từ mỗi chi tộc, ra trận, họ và Phi-nê-a con trai thầy tế lễ Ê-lê-a-sa, ra trận, và các vật dụng thánh và các kèn để báo động [ở] trong tay người.
vi.B: Môi-se sai họ ra trận, mỗi chi tộc một nghìn người, cùng với Phi-nê-a con trai thầy tế lễ Ê-lê-a-sa. Phi-nê-a cầm theo các vật dụng thánh và các kèn để thổi báo động.
vi.R: Môi-se sai họ ra trận, mỗi chi tộc một nghìn người. Ông cũng sai Phi-nê-a, con trai thầy tế lễ Ê-lê-a-sa, đi theo. Phi-nê-a mang theo các vật dụng thánh và các kèn để thổi báo động.

ko.L: 그리고 모세는 지파마다 천 [명]씩 그들을 전쟁에 보냈는데, 그들과 제사장 엘르아살의 아들 비느하스를 전쟁에 [보냈고], 성소의 기구들과 경보용 나팔들이 그의 손에 [있었다].
ko.B: 모세는 지파마다 천 명씩 뽑힌 그들을 전쟁에 보내면서, 제사장 엘르아살의 아들 비느하스도 함께 보냈다. 비느하스는 성소의 거룩한 기구들과 경보를 울리는 나팔들을 맡았다.
ko.R: 모세는 지파마다 천 명씩 뽑힌 사람들을 싸움터로 보냈다. 제사장 엘르아살의 아들 비느하스도 함께 보냈다. 비느하스는 성소의 거룩한 물건들과 경보를 알리는 나팔들을 가지고 갔다.

pt.L: E Moisés os enviou, mil por tribo, à guerra, a eles e a Fineias, filho do sacerdote Eleazar, à guerra; e os utensílios sagrados e as trombetas do alarme [estavam] na sua mão.
pt.B: Moisés os enviou à guerra, mil de cada tribo, junto com Fineias, filho do sacerdote Eleazar, que levava consigo os utensílios sagrados e as trombetas para dar o alarme.
pt.R: Moisés mandou para a guerra mil homens de cada tribo. Mandou também Fineias, filho do sacerdote Eleazar. Fineias levou com ele os objetos sagrados e as trombetas para dar o sinal de alarme.

decisions.choice: Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest: Phinehas goes, not the high priest himself
decisions.reason: "The priest" belongs to Eleazar, Aaron's successor (20:25-28). The high priest was not to come near the dead (Leviticus 21:10-12), and Phinehas had already acted for the LORD against the sin at Peor (25:7-13), so he is the fitting priest to go with the army.

decisions.choice: the holy articles: sacred objects from the sanctuary, perhaps the ark
decisions.reason: The phrase means articles that belong to the holy place. It could mean the ark, which went before Israel in battle in other places (10:35; 14:44; 1 Samuel 4:3-4), or other sacred objects, such as the priest's garments or the means of asking the LORD's will. The text does not say which.

decisions.choice: the trumpets for the alarm: the silver trumpets of 10:1-10
decisions.reason: The LORD had told the priests to sound the alarm on the silver trumpets when Israel went to war, "so that you will be remembered before the LORD your God" (10:9).

decisions.choice: who had in his care / Phinehas took with him
decisions.reason: Hebrew ends with "in his hand". Balanced and Readable make it clear that "his" is Phinehas, the one who carried them.

decisions.choice: "성소의 기구들" for the holy articles and "경보용 나팔" / "경보를 울리는 나팔" for the trumpets for the alarm
decisions.reason: "기구" is the word Korean Exodus and Numbers use for the sanctuary's articles; the trumpets are the silver trumpets of 10:1-10 (meaning decision).

source.text: וַֽיִּצְבְּאוּ֙ עַל־מִדְיָ֔ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיַּֽהַרְג֖וּ כָּל־זָכָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And they warred against Midian, as commanded Yahweh Moses, and they killed every male.

en.L: And they waged war against Midian, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses, and they killed every male.
en.B: They made war on Midian, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses, and killed every man.
en.R: They fought against Midian, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses, and they killed all the men.

es.L: Y guerrearon contra Madián, como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había mandado a Moisés, y mataron a todo varón.
es.B: Hicieron la guerra a Madián, como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había mandado a Moisés, y mataron a todos los hombres.
es.R: Pelearon contra Madián, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se lo había ordenado a Moisés, y mataron a todos los hombres.

fr.L: Et ils firent la guerre contre Madian, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait ordonné à Moïse, et ils tuèrent tout mâle.
fr.B: Ils combattirent Madian, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait ordonné à Moïse, et tuèrent tous les hommes.
fr.R: Ils ont combattu contre Madian, exactement comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait ordonné à Moïse, et ils ont tué tous les hommes.

sw.L: Wakapigana vita dhidi ya Midiani, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyomwamuru Musa, wakamuua kila mwanamume.
sw.B: Walipigana vita na Midiani, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyomwamuru Musa, wakawaua wanaume wote.
sw.R: Walipigana na Midiani, sawasawa na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyomwamuru Musa, wakawaua wanaume wote.

vi.L: Và họ giao chiến với Ma-đi-an, như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền cho Môi-se, và họ giết mọi người nam.
vi.B: Họ giao chiến với Ma-đi-an như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền cho Môi-se, và giết hết đàn ông.
vi.R: Họ chiến đấu với Ma-đi-an, đúng như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền cho Môi-se, và giết hết đàn ông.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 명령하신 대로 미디안과 싸워서 모든 남자를 죽였다.
ko.B: 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 명령하신 대로 미디안과 싸워서 남자를 모두 죽였다.
ko.R: 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 명령하신 대로 미디안과 싸웠고, 남자들을 모두 죽였다.

pt.L: E guerrearam contra Midiã, como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha ordenado a Moisés, e mataram todo macho.
pt.B: Eles fizeram guerra contra Midiã, como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha ordenado a Moisés, e mataram todos os homens.
pt.R: Eles lutaram contra Midiã, exatamente como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha ordenado a Moisés, e mataram todos os homens.

decisions.choice: every male: every man of fighting age among those they fought
decisions.reason: Verse 17 shows that the boys were still alive when the army came back, so "every male" here means the men they met in battle. Midian did not disappear; it is a strong people again in Gideon's time (Judges 6:1-6).

decisions.choice: every man / all the men
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "man", since the boys are dealt with separately in verse 17. Literal keeps "male".

decisions.choice: todo macho (L); todos os homens (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word for "male", as the English Literal does, because verse 17 turns to the boys; "varão" is archaic. Balanced and Readable say "homens" (m1).

source.text: וְאֶת־מַלְכֵ֨י מִדְיָ֜ן הָרְג֣וּ עַל־חַלְלֵיהֶ֗ם אֶת־אֱוִ֤י וְאֶת־רֶ֨קֶם֙ וְאֶת־צ֤וּר וְאֶת־חוּר֙ וְאֶת־רֶ֔בַע חֲמֵ֖שֶׁת מַלְכֵ֣י מִדְיָ֑ן וְאֵת֙ בִּלְעָ֣ם בֶּן־בְּע֔וֹר הָרְג֖וּ בֶּחָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And kings of Midian they killed upon their slain: Evi and Rekem and Zur and Hur and Reba, five kings of Midian; and Balaam son of Beor they killed with the sword.

en.L: And they killed the kings of Midian with their slain: Evi and Rekem and Zur and Hur and Reba, the five kings of Midian; and Balaam son of Beor they killed with the sword.
en.B: Along with the others who were killed, they killed the kings of Midian, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba, the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword.
en.R: Among those they killed were the five kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with a sword.

es.L: Y a los reyes de Madián mataron junto con sus muertos: a Evi, y a Requem, y a Zur, y a Hur, y a Reba, los cinco reyes de Madián; y a Balaam hijo de Beor lo mataron a espada.
es.B: Junto con los demás que murieron, mataron a los reyes de Madián, Evi, Requem, Zur, Hur y Reba, los cinco reyes de Madián. También mataron a espada a Balaam hijo de Beor.
es.R: Entre los que mataron estaban los cinco reyes de Madián: Evi, Requem, Zur, Hur y Reba. También mataron a Balaam, hijo de Beor, con una espada.

fr.L: Et les rois de Madian, ils les tuèrent avec leurs morts : Évi, et Rékem, et Tsour, et Hour, et Réba, les cinq rois de Madian ; et Balaam fils de Béor, ils le tuèrent par l’épée.
fr.B: Avec les autres qui furent tués, ils tuèrent les rois de Madian, Évi, Rékem, Tsour, Hour et Réba, les cinq rois de Madian. Ils tuèrent aussi par l’épée Balaam fils de Béor.
fr.R: Parmi ceux qu’ils ont tués, il y avait les cinq rois de Madian : Évi, Rékem, Tsour, Hour et Réba. Ils ont aussi tué Balaam, fils de Béor, avec l’épée.

sw.L: Na wafalme wa Midiani wakawaua pamoja na waliouawa wao: Evi, na Rekemu, na Suri, na Huri, na Reba, wafalme watano wa Midiani; na Balaamu mwana wa Beori wakamuua kwa upanga.
sw.B: Pamoja na wengine waliouawa, waliwaua wafalme wa Midiani, Evi, Rekemu, Suri, Huri na Reba, wafalme watano wa Midiani. Pia walimuua Balaamu mwana wa Beori kwa upanga.
sw.R: Miongoni mwa waliowaua walikuwa wafalme watano wa Midiani: Evi, Rekemu, Suri, Huri na Reba. Pia walimuua Balaamu mwana wa Beori kwa upanga.

vi.L: Và họ giết các vua Ma-đi-an cùng với những người bị giết của họ: Ê-vi, Rê-kem, Xu-rơ, Hu-rơ và Rê-ba, năm vua Ma-đi-an; và Ba-la-am con trai Bê-ô, họ giết bằng gươm.
vi.B: Cùng với những người khác bị giết, họ giết các vua Ma-đi-an là Ê-vi, Rê-kem, Xu-rơ, Hu-rơ và Rê-ba, năm vua Ma-đi-an. Họ cũng giết Ba-la-am con trai Bê-ô bằng gươm.
vi.R: Trong số những người bị giết có năm vua Ma-đi-an: Ê-vi, Rê-kem, Xu-rơ, Hu-rơ và Rê-ba. Họ cũng dùng gươm giết Ba-la-am con trai Bê-ô.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 그들이 죽인 자들과 함께 미디안의 왕들, 곧 에위와 레겜과 수르와 훌과 레바, 미디안의 다섯 왕을 죽였다. 그리고 브올의 아들 발람도 칼로 죽였다.
ko.B: 그들은 다른 사람들과 함께 미디안의 왕들도 죽였는데, 그들은 에위와 레겜과 수르와 훌과 레바, 곧 미디안의 다섯 왕이었다. 그들은 브올의 아들 발람도 칼로 죽였다.
ko.R: 그들이 죽인 사람들 가운데에는 미디안의 다섯 왕, 곧 에위와 레겜과 수르와 훌과 레바도 있었다. 그들은 브올의 아들 발람도 칼로 죽였다.

pt.L: E mataram os reis de Midiã com os seus mortos: Evi, e Requém, e Zur, e Hur, e Reba, os cinco reis de Midiã; e Balaão, filho de Beor, mataram à espada.
pt.B: Junto com os outros que foram mortos, mataram os reis de Midiã: Evi, Requém, Zur, Hur e Reba, os cinco reis de Midiã. Mataram também à espada Balaão, filho de Beor.
pt.R: Entre os mortos estavam os cinco reis de Midiã: Evi, Requém, Zur, Hur e Reba. Mataram também Balaão, filho de Beor, com a espada.

decisions.choice: with their slain: in addition to the others killed
decisions.reason: The phrase means "on top of" or "along with" the rest of the dead: the kings fell in the same battle as their men.

decisions.choice: Zur: the father of Cozbi
decisions.reason: Zur is named in 25:15 as the father of Cozbi, the Midianite woman killed at Peor, and as the head of a family in Midian. Joshua 13:21 calls these five men chiefs of Midian, allied with Sihon king of the Amorites.

decisions.choice: Balaam son of Beor: the prophet of chapters 22-24, killed among the Midianites
decisions.reason: Balaam had gone home after blessing Israel (24:25), but here he is found with Midian. Verse 16 explains why: his advice led Israel into the sin at Peor.

decisions.choice: the verb first
decisions.reason: Hebrew puts the kings first for emphasis and says "they killed" twice; English puts the verb first and lists the names after it.

decisions.choice: "Ê-vi, Rê-kem, Xu-rơ, Hu-rơ, Rê-ba"
decisions.reason: The forms of the Vietnamese Joshua 13:21; Hur the Midianite king keeps the same Vietnamese form as Hur in Exodus.

decisions.choice: Names in the usual Protestant Korean forms: "에위", "레겜", "수르", "훌", "레바"; "브올의 아들 발람"
decisions.reason: "발람" is the term sheet form and "브올" the form Korean 1 Chronicles 1:43 uses for Beor; the kings keep the forms Korean readers know, the same in Joshua 13:21.

decisions.choice: Evi, Requém, Zur, Hur, Reba
decisions.reason: The five kings take their usual Brazilian forms; "Zur" is the same man as in 25:15, the father of Cozbi (m2).

source.text: וַיִּשְׁבּ֧וּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶת־נְשֵׁ֥י מִדְיָ֖ן וְאֶת־טַפָּ֑ם וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־בְּהֶמְתָּ֧ם וְאֶת־כָּל־מִקְנֵהֶ֛ם וְאֶת־כָּל־חֵילָ֖ם בָּזָֽזוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And took captive [the] sons of Israel [the] women of Midian and their little ones, and all their cattle and all their livestock and all their wealth they plundered.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel took captive the women of Midian and their little ones, and all their cattle and all their livestock and all their goods they plundered.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} took the women of Midian and their children captive, and they carried off all their cattle, all their flocks and all their goods as plunder.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} captured the Midianite women and children. They took all their animals, their flocks, and everything they owned.

es.L: Y los hijos de Israel llevaron en cautiverio a las mujeres de Madián y a sus pequeños, y todo su ganado y todos sus rebaños y todos sus bienes saquearon.
es.B: Los israelitas tomaron cautivos a las mujeres de Madián y a sus niños, y se llevaron como botín todo su ganado, todos sus rebaños y todos sus bienes.
es.R: Los israelitas capturaron a las mujeres y a los niños de Madián. Se llevaron todos sus animales, sus rebaños y todo lo que tenían.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël emmenèrent en captivité les femmes de Madian et leurs petits enfants, et tout leur bétail, et tous leurs troupeaux, et tous leurs biens, ils les pillèrent.
fr.B: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} emmenèrent en captivité les femmes de Madian et leurs enfants, et ils emportèrent comme butin tout leur bétail, tous leurs troupeaux et tous leurs biens.
fr.R: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont capturé les femmes et les enfants de Madian. Ils ont pris tous leurs animaux, leurs troupeaux et tout ce qu’ils possédaient.

sw.L: Na wana wa Israeli wakawachukua mateka wanawake wa Midiani na watoto wao wadogo, na mifugo yao yote, na makundi yao yote, na mali zao zote wakateka nyara.
sw.B: Waisraeli waliwachukua mateka wanawake wa Midiani na watoto wao, wakachukua nyara mifugo yao yote, makundi yao yote na mali zao zote.
sw.R: Waisraeli waliwateka wanawake na watoto wa Midiani. Walichukua wanyama wao wote, makundi yao na kila kitu walichokuwa nacho.

vi.L: Và con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên bắt các phụ nữ Ma-đi-an và con nhỏ của họ làm phu tù, và tất cả súc vật, tất cả bầy gia súc và tất cả của cải của họ, họ cướp lấy.
vi.B: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên bắt phụ nữ và trẻ con Ma-đi-an làm phu tù, và cướp lấy tất cả bò, tất cả bầy chiên dê và mọi của cải của họ.
vi.R: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên bắt phụ nữ và trẻ con Ma-đi-an. Họ lấy hết súc vật, bầy chiên dê và mọi thứ người Ma-đi-an có.

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘 자손이 미디안의 여자들과 그들의 어린아이들을 사로잡고, 그들의 모든 짐승과 그들의 모든 가축과 그들의 모든 재물을 약탈했다.
ko.B: 이스라엘 백성은 미디안의 여자들과 아이들을 사로잡고, 그들의 소 떼와 양 떼와 재물을 모두 빼앗았다.
ko.R: 이스라엘 사람들은 미디안 여자들과 아이들을 사로잡았다. 그리고 그들의 짐승과 양 떼와 가진 것을 모두 빼앗았다.

pt.L: E os filhos de Israel levaram cativas as mulheres de Midiã e os seus pequeninos, e todo o seu gado, e todos os seus rebanhos, e todos os seus bens saquearam.
pt.B: Os israelitas levaram cativas as mulheres de Midiã e os seus filhos pequenos, e tomaram como despojo todo o seu gado, todos os seus rebanhos e todos os seus bens.
pt.R: Os israelitas capturaram as mulheres e as crianças de Midiã. Levaram todos os animais, os rebanhos e tudo o que eles tinham.

decisions.choice: cattle, livestock: the larger animals and the herds and flocks
decisions.reason: The first word covers domestic animals in general, the second livestock owned as wealth. Together they mean all the animals, which verses 32-34 list as sheep, cattle and donkeys.

decisions.choice: goods: wealth and possessions of every kind
decisions.reason: The word means strength, and so also wealth; here it covers all that the Midianites owned, including the gold of verse 50.

decisions.choice: children
decisions.reason: The word means the little ones of a household. Balanced and Readable say "children"; Literal keeps "little ones".

source.text: וְאֵ֤ת כָּל־עָרֵיהֶם֙ בְּמ֣וֹשְׁבֹתָ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־טִֽירֹתָ֑ם שָׂרְפ֖וּ בָּאֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And all their cities in their dwelling places and all their encampments they burned with fire.

en.L: And all their cities in their dwelling places and all their encampments they burned with fire.
en.B: They burned all the towns where the Midianites lived, and all their camps.
en.R: They burned down all the towns where the Midianites lived and all their camps.

es.L: Y todas sus ciudades en sus lugares de habitación y todos sus campamentos quemaron con fuego.
es.B: Quemaron todas las ciudades donde vivían los madianitas y todos sus campamentos.
es.R: Incendiaron todas las ciudades donde vivían los madianitas y todos sus campamentos.

fr.L: Et toutes leurs villes dans leurs lieux d’habitation et tous leurs campements, ils les brûlèrent par le feu.
fr.B: Ils brûlèrent toutes les villes où habitaient les Madianites, ainsi que tous leurs campements.
fr.R: Ils ont brûlé toutes les villes où vivaient les Madianites, et tous leurs camps.

sw.L: Na miji yao yote katika makao yao na kambi zao zote wakaiteketeza kwa moto.
sw.B: Waliiteketeza kwa moto miji yote waliyoishi Wamidiani, pamoja na kambi zao zote.
sw.R: Waliichoma moto miji yote ambamo Wamidiani waliishi, na kambi zao zote.

vi.L: Và tất cả các thành của họ trong các nơi ở của họ và tất cả các đồn trại của họ, họ đốt bằng lửa.
vi.B: Họ đốt hết các thành nơi người Ma-đi-an sinh sống và mọi đồn trại của họ.
vi.R: Họ đốt cháy hết các thành nơi người Ma-đi-an sinh sống và mọi trại của họ.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 살던 곳의 그들의 모든 성읍과 그들의 모든 진영을 불로 태웠다.
ko.B: 그들은 미디안 사람들이 살던 성읍들과 진영들을 모두 불태웠다.
ko.R: 그들은 미디안 사람들이 살던 마을과 천막촌을 모두 불태워 버렸다.

pt.L: E todas as suas cidades nas suas moradas e todos os seus acampamentos queimaram a fogo.
pt.B: Queimaram todas as cidades onde os midianitas moravam e todos os seus acampamentos.
pt.R: Puseram fogo em todas as cidades onde os midianitas moravam e em todos os seus acampamentos.

decisions.choice: encampments: walled camps or settlements of tent dwellers
decisions.reason: The word names a circle of tents or a walled enclosure, the kind of settlement used by herding peoples (Genesis 25:16, of the sons of Ishmael). The Midianites lived both in towns and in such camps.

decisions.choice: where the Midianites lived
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Midianites for the "they" of the Hebrew, which is clear in the context.

decisions.choice: "진영" (Literal, Balanced), "천막촌" (Readable) for "encampments"
decisions.reason: The word is a walled camp or settlement of tent dwellers (meaning decision); "진" is kept for Israel's own camp, so the Midianite camps are "진영", and Readable says what they were.

source.text: וַיִּקְחוּ֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַשָּׁלָ֔ל וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־הַמַּלְק֑וֹחַ בָּאָדָ֖ם וּבַבְּהֵמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they took all the spoil and all the booty, of humankind and of livestock.

en.L: And they took all the spoil and all the booty, of people and of animals.
en.B: They took all the spoil and all the plunder, both people and animals.
en.R: They took everything they had captured, both people and animals.

es.L: Y tomaron todo el botín y toda la presa, de personas y de animales.
es.B: Tomaron todo el botín y toda la presa, tanto personas como animales.
es.R: Se llevaron todo lo que habían capturado, tanto personas como animales.

fr.L: Et ils prirent tout le butin et toutes les prises, en personnes et en bêtes.
fr.B: Ils prirent tout le butin et toutes les prises, personnes comme animaux.
fr.R: Ils ont pris tout ce qu’ils avaient capturé, les gens comme les animaux.

sw.L: Nao wakachukua nyara zote na mawindo yote, ya watu na ya wanyama.
sw.B: Walichukua nyara zote na mawindo yote, watu na wanyama pia.
sw.R: Walichukua kila kitu walichokuwa wameteka, watu pamoja na wanyama.

vi.L: Và họ lấy tất cả chiến lợi phẩm và tất cả của cướp được, cả người lẫn súc vật.
vi.B: Họ lấy tất cả chiến lợi phẩm và của cướp được, cả người lẫn súc vật.
vi.R: Họ đem theo mọi thứ đã chiếm được, cả người lẫn súc vật.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 사람과 짐승을 [가리지 않고] 모든 노략물과 모든 전리품을 가져갔다.
ko.B: 그들은 사람이든 짐승이든 노략물과 전리품을 모두 가져갔다.
ko.R: 그들은 사로잡은 것을 사람이든 짐승이든 모두 데려갔다.

pt.L: E tomaram todo o despojo e toda a presa, de gente e de animais.
pt.B: Tomaram todo o despojo e toda a presa, tanto pessoas como animais.
pt.R: Levaram tudo o que tinham capturado, tanto pessoas como animais.

decisions.choice: spoil and booty: what was taken in war, goods and living captives
decisions.reason: The two words overlap. The first is the general word for what is taken from a defeated enemy; the second, from the verb "to take", is used in this chapter for what was captured alive, people and animals (verses 12, 26, 32).

decisions.choice: plunder
decisions.reason: Balanced says "spoil" and "plunder" for the two words throughout the chapter; Literal keeps "booty" for the second. Readable uses one plain phrase for both.

decisions.choice: el botín / la presa
decisions.reason: The chapter's two words for what was taken stay apart throughout: "botín" for the general word (shalal), "presa" for what was captured alive (malqoach); the verb bazaz is "saquear" and the captives are "cautivos".

decisions.choice: le butin / les prises
decisions.reason: The chapter's two words for what was taken stay apart throughout: "butin" for the general word (shalal), "prises" for what was captured alive (malqoach); the verb bazaz is "piller" and the captives are "captifs".

decisions.choice: nyara / mawindo
decisions.reason: The chapter's two words for what was taken stay apart throughout: "nyara" for the general word (shalal), "mawindo" for what was captured alive (malqoach); the captives are "mateka" and the verb bazaz is "kuteka nyara".

decisions.choice: "노략물" for the spoil and "전리품" for the booty
decisions.reason: The two words cover what was taken in war, goods and living captives (meaning decision); Korean has two current words to keep the pair.

decisions.choice: o despojo; a presa
decisions.reason: For the chapter: the two Hebrew words (m1) are "o despojo", what is taken from a defeated enemy, and "a presa", what is captured alive, at Literal and Balanced, so that the reader can follow them through verses 12-53; Readable uses one plain phrase, as the English does.

source.text: וַיָּבִ֡אוּ אֶל־מֹשֶׁה֩ וְאֶל־אֶלְעָזָ֨ר הַכֹּהֵ֜ן וְאֶל־עֲדַ֣ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶת־הַשְּׁבִ֧י וְאֶת־הַמַּלְק֛וֹחַ וְאֶת־הַשָּׁלָ֖ל אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה אֶל־עַֽרְבֹ֣ת מוֹאָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־יַרְדֵּ֥ן יְרֵחֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they brought to Moses and to Eleazar the priest and to [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel the captives and the booty and the spoil, to the camp, to [the] plains of Moab which [are] by [the] Jordan [of] Jericho.

en.L: And they brought the captives and the booty and the spoil to Moses and to Eleazar the priest and to the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, to the camp on the plains of Moab, which [are] by the Jordan [across from] Jericho.
en.B: They brought the captives, the plunder and the spoil to Moses, to Eleazar the priest and to the congregation of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, at the camp on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho.
en.R: They brought the captives and everything else they had taken to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the community of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. Israel was camped on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan River across from Jericho.

es.L: Y trajeron los cautivos y la presa y el botín a Moisés y a Eleazar el sacerdote y a la comunidad de los hijos de Israel, al campamento, a las llanuras de Moab, que [están] junto al Jordán, [frente a] Jericó.
es.B: Llevaron los cautivos, la presa y el botín a Moisés, a Eleazar el sacerdote y a la comunidad de los israelitas, al campamento en las llanuras de Moab, junto al Jordán, frente a Jericó.
es.R: Llevaron a los cautivos y todo lo demás que habían tomado a Moisés, a Eleazar el sacerdote y a la comunidad de los israelitas. Israel estaba acampado en la llanura de Moab, a orillas del río Jordán, frente a Jericó.

fr.L: Et ils amenèrent les captifs, et les prises, et le butin à Moïse, et à Éléazar le prêtre, et à la communauté des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, au camp, dans les plaines de Moab, qui [sont] près du Jourdain, [en face de] Jéricho.
fr.B: Ils amenèrent les captifs, les prises et le butin à Moïse, à Éléazar le prêtre et à la communauté des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, au camp, dans les plaines de Moab, près du Jourdain, en face de Jéricho.
fr.R: Ils ont amené les captifs et tout ce qu’ils avaient pris à Moïse, à Éléazar le prêtre et à la communauté des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}. Israël campait dans la plaine de Moab, au bord du Jourdain, en face de Jéricho.

sw.L: Nao wakawaleta mateka, na mawindo, na nyara kwa Musa, na kwa Eleazari kuhani, na kwa jumuiya ya wana wa Israeli, kambini, katika nchi tambarare za Moabu, zilizo karibu na Yordani [mkabala na] Yeriko.
sw.B: Waliwaleta mateka, mawindo na nyara kwa Musa, kwa Eleazari kuhani na kwa jumuiya ya Waisraeli, kambini katika nchi tambarare za Moabu, karibu na Yordani, mkabala na Yeriko.
sw.R: Waliwaleta mateka na vitu vingine vyote walivyoteka kwa Musa, kwa Eleazari kuhani na kwa jumuiya ya Waisraeli. Israeli walikuwa wamepiga kambi katika nchi tambarare ya Moabu, kando ya Mto Yordani, mkabala na Yeriko.

vi.L: Và họ đem các phu tù, của cướp và chiến lợi phẩm đến Môi-se và thầy tế lễ Ê-lê-a-sa và hội chúng con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên, tại trại quân ở các đồng bằng Mô-áp, bên sông Giô-đanh [đối diện] Giê-ri-cô.
vi.B: Họ đem các phu tù, của cướp và chiến lợi phẩm đến cho Môi-se, thầy tế lễ Ê-lê-a-sa và hội chúng Y-sơ-ra-ên, tại trại quân trong các đồng bằng Mô-áp, bên sông Giô-đanh, đối diện Giê-ri-cô.
vi.R: Họ đem các phu tù và mọi thứ khác đã chiếm được đến cho Môi-se, thầy tế lễ Ê-lê-a-sa và cộng đồng dân Y-sơ-ra-ên. Lúc ấy Y-sơ-ra-ên đang đóng trại trong các đồng bằng Mô-áp, bên sông Giô-đanh, đối diện Giê-ri-cô.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 포로들과 전리품과 노략물을 모세와 제사장 엘르아살과 이스라엘 자손의 회중에게로, 여리고 [맞은편] 요단강 가에 있는 모압 평지의 진으로 가져왔다.
ko.B: 그들은 포로들과 전리품과 노략물을 모세와 제사장 엘르아살과 이스라엘 백성의 회중에게 가져왔다. 그곳은 요단강 가, 여리고 맞은편 모압 평지에 있는 진이었다.
ko.R: 그들은 포로들과 빼앗은 것을 모두 모세와 제사장 엘르아살과 이스라엘 사람들의 회중에게 가져왔다. 이스라엘은 그때 여리고 맞은편, 요단강 가의 모압 평지에 진을 치고 있었다.

pt.L: E trouxeram a Moisés, e ao sacerdote Eleazar, e à comunidade dos filhos de Israel os cativos, e a presa, e o despojo, ao acampamento, nas planícies de Moabe, que [estão] junto ao Jordão, [em frente de] Jericó.
pt.B: Levaram os cativos, a presa e o despojo a Moisés, ao sacerdote Eleazar e à comunidade dos israelitas, no acampamento, nas planícies de Moabe, junto ao Jordão, em frente de Jericó.
pt.R: Eles levaram os cativos e tudo o mais que tinham tomado a Moisés, ao sacerdote Eleazar e à comunidade dos israelitas. Israel estava acampado nas planícies de Moabe, junto ao rio Jordão, em frente de Jericó.

decisions.choice: the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho: Israel's last camp before the crossing
decisions.reason: Israel camped here on the east side of the Jordan, facing Jericho on the other side (22:1; 26:3). The phrase "the Jordan of Jericho" means the stretch of the river opposite that city.

decisions.choice: across from Jericho
decisions.reason: Hebrew says only "the Jordan of Jericho". Literal brackets "across from"; Balanced and Readable say it plainly, as in 22:1.

decisions.choice: "모압 평지", "요단강", "여리고 맞은편"
decisions.reason: "모압 평지" is the form Korean Joshua 13:32 uses; "요단강" without a space as settled for these books; "맞은편" says that Jericho lay across the river (meaning decision), and Literal brackets it, as the English does.

source.text: וַיֵּ֨צְא֜וּ מֹשֶׁ֨ה וְאֶלְעָזָ֧ר הַכֹּהֵ֛ן וְכָל־נְשִׂיאֵ֥י הָעֵדָ֖ה לִקְרָאתָ֑ם אֶל־מִח֖וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out Moses and Eleazar the priest and all [the] leaders of the congregation to meet them, to outside of the camp.

en.L: And Moses and Eleazar the priest and all the leaders of the congregation went out to meet them outside the camp.
en.B: Moses, Eleazar the priest and all the leaders of the congregation went out to meet them outside the camp.
en.R: Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the community went out of the camp to meet them.

es.L: Y salieron Moisés y Eleazar el sacerdote y todos los jefes de la comunidad a recibirlos fuera del campamento.
es.B: Moisés, Eleazar el sacerdote y todos los jefes de la comunidad salieron a recibirlos fuera del campamento.
es.R: Moisés, Eleazar el sacerdote y todos los jefes de la comunidad salieron del campamento para recibirlos.

fr.L: Et Moïse et Éléazar le prêtre et tous les chefs de la communauté sortirent à leur rencontre, hors du camp.
fr.B: Moïse, Éléazar le prêtre et tous les chefs de la communauté sortirent à leur rencontre hors du camp.
fr.R: Moïse, Éléazar le prêtre et tous les chefs de la communauté sont sortis du camp pour aller à leur rencontre.

sw.L: Na Musa na Eleazari kuhani na viongozi wote wa jumuiya wakatoka kwenda kuwalaki nje ya kambi.
sw.B: Musa, Eleazari kuhani na viongozi wote wa jumuiya walitoka kwenda kuwalaki nje ya kambi.
sw.R: Musa, Eleazari kuhani na viongozi wote wa jumuiya walitoka nje ya kambi kwenda kuwapokea.

vi.L: Và Môi-se, thầy tế lễ Ê-lê-a-sa và tất cả các thủ lĩnh của hội chúng đi ra đón họ bên ngoài trại quân.
vi.B: Môi-se, thầy tế lễ Ê-lê-a-sa và tất cả các thủ lĩnh của hội chúng đi ra đón họ bên ngoài trại quân.
vi.R: Môi-se, thầy tế lễ Ê-lê-a-sa và tất cả các thủ lĩnh của cộng đồng ra khỏi khu trại để đón họ.

ko.L: 그리고 모세와 제사장 엘르아살과 회중의 모든 지도자들이 그들을 맞으러 진 밖으로 나갔다.
ko.B: 모세와 제사장 엘르아살과 회중의 모든 지도자들이 그들을 맞으러 진 밖으로 나갔다.
ko.R: 모세와 제사장 엘르아살과 회중의 모든 지도자들이 그들을 맞으려고 진 밖으로 나갔다.

pt.L: E Moisés, e o sacerdote Eleazar, e todos os líderes da comunidade saíram ao encontro deles, para fora do acampamento.
pt.B: Moisés, o sacerdote Eleazar e todos os líderes da comunidade saíram para recebê-los fora do acampamento.
pt.R: Moisés, o sacerdote Eleazar e todos os líderes da comunidade saíram do acampamento para encontrar os soldados.

decisions.choice: outside the camp: the returning army could not yet enter
decisions.reason: Anyone who had touched the dead was unclean for seven days and had to stay out of the camp, so that the camp where the LORD lived among his people would not be made unclean (5:2-3; 19:11-13). The leaders go out to the soldiers; the soldiers do not come in (verses 19, 24).

source.text: וַיִּקְצֹ֣ף מֹשֶׁ֔ה עַ֖ל פְּקוּדֵ֣י הֶחָ֑יִל שָׂרֵ֤י הָאֲלָפִים֙ וְשָׂרֵ֣י הַמֵּא֔וֹת הַבָּאִ֖ים מִצְּבָ֥א הַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And was angry Moses at [the] officers of the army, [the] commanders of the thousands and [the] commanders of the hundreds, the [ones] coming from [the] service of the battle.

en.L: And Moses was angry with the officers of the army, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, who came from the service of the battle.
en.B: Moses was angry with the officers of the army, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, who were coming back from the battle.
en.R: But Moses was angry with the army officers, the men who commanded a thousand soldiers or a hundred soldiers. They were coming back from the battle.

es.L: Y se enojó Moisés contra los oficiales del ejército, los jefes de millares y los jefes de centenas, que venían del servicio de la batalla.
es.B: Moisés se enojó con los oficiales del ejército, los jefes de millares y los jefes de centenas, que volvían de la batalla.
es.R: Pero Moisés se enojó con los oficiales del ejército, los hombres que mandaban a mil soldados o a cien soldados. Ellos volvían de la batalla.

fr.L: Et Moïse s’irrita contre les officiers de l’armée, les chefs de milliers et les chefs de centaines, qui revenaient du service de la bataille.
fr.B: Moïse s’irrita contre les officiers de l’armée, les chefs de milliers et les chefs de centaines, qui revenaient du combat.
fr.R: Mais Moïse s’est mis en colère contre les officiers de l’armée, les hommes qui commandaient mille soldats ou cent soldats. Ils revenaient de la bataille.

sw.L: Naye Musa akawakasirikia maafisa wa jeshi, wakuu wa maelfu na wakuu wa mamia, waliokuwa wakirudi kutoka utumishi wa vita.
sw.B: Musa aliwakasirikia maafisa wa jeshi, wakuu wa maelfu na wakuu wa mamia, waliokuwa wakirudi kutoka vitani.
sw.R: Lakini Musa aliwakasirikia maafisa wa jeshi, wanaume walioongoza askari elfu moja au askari mia moja. Walikuwa wakirudi kutoka vitani.

vi.L: Và Môi-se nổi giận với các sĩ quan của quân đội, các quan chỉ huy ngàn quân và các quan chỉ huy trăm quân, là những người trở về từ việc chiến trận.
vi.B: Môi-se nổi giận với các sĩ quan của quân đội, các quan chỉ huy ngàn quân và các quan chỉ huy trăm quân, là những người vừa trở về từ trận chiến.
vi.R: Nhưng Môi-se nổi giận với các sĩ quan trong quân đội, là những người chỉ huy một nghìn lính hay một trăm lính. Họ đang từ trận chiến trở về.

ko.L: 그리고 모세가 군대의 지휘관들, 곧 전쟁에 나갔다가 돌아오는 천부장들과 백부장들에게 화를 냈다.
ko.B: 모세는 싸움에서 돌아오는 군대의 지휘관들, 곧 천부장들과 백부장들에게 화를 냈다.
ko.R: 그러나 모세는 싸움터에서 돌아오는 군대 지휘관들, 곧 천 명을 거느린 사람들과 백 명을 거느린 사람들에게 화를 냈다.

pt.L: E Moisés se irou contra os oficiais do exército, os chefes de mil e os chefes de cem, que vinham do serviço da batalha.
pt.B: Moisés ficou irado com os oficiais do exército, os chefes de mil e os chefes de cem, que voltavam da batalha.
pt.R: Mas Moisés ficou irado com os oficiais do exército, os homens que comandavam mil soldados ou cem soldados. Eles estavam voltando da batalha.

decisions.choice: commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds: the ranks of officers in the army
decisions.reason: The army was divided into units of a thousand and of a hundred, each with its commander, as in the leaders Moses set over the people (Exodus 18:21, 25). Here "thousands" is a military unit; with twelve thousand men in all, there would be twelve units of a thousand.

decisions.choice: But / soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable adds "but" to show the turn from the welcome of verse 13 to Moses' anger, and says plainly what the ranks were.

decisions.choice: los jefes de millares y los jefes de centenas
alternatives: los capitanes de mil y de cien
decisions.reason: The same titles as for the leaders Moses appointed in Exodus 18:21, 25; Readable says what they commanded.

decisions.choice: les chefs de milliers et les chefs de centaines
alternatives: les commandants de mille et de cent hommes
decisions.reason: The same titles as for the leaders Moses appointed in Exodus 18:21, 25, so that the reader sees the same ranks; Readable says what they commanded.

decisions.choice: wakuu wa maelfu na wakuu wa mamia
alternatives: makamanda wa elfu na wa mia
decisions.reason: The same titles as for the leaders Moses appointed in Exodus 18:21, 25; Readable says what they commanded.

decisions.choice: "các quan chỉ huy ngàn quân và các quan chỉ huy trăm quân"
decisions.reason: The ranks as the Vietnamese Chronicles names them.

decisions.choice: "천부장", "백부장" (Literal, Balanced); "천 명을 거느린 사람", "백 명을 거느린 사람" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The ranks of officers in the army (meaning decision); "천부장" and "백부장" are the Korean words for these ranks, and Readable spells out what they mean.

decisions.choice: os chefes de mil e os chefes de cem
alternatives: os comandantes de milhares e de centenas
decisions.reason: As Exodus 18:21, 25 names the same ranks (m1): "chefes de mil", "chefes de cem". Readable says what the ranks were, as the English Readable does.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מֹשֶׁ֑ה הַֽחִיִּיתֶ֖ם כָּל־נְקֵבָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to them Moses, have you let live every female?

en.L: And Moses said to them, "Have you let every female live?
en.B: Moses said to them, "You have let all the women live?
en.R: Moses said to them, "You let all the women live?

es.L: Y les dijo Moisés: «¿{{plural_you:Han dejado|Habéis dejado}} con vida a toda hembra?
es.B: Moisés les dijo: «¿Así que {{plural_you:dejaron|dejasteis}} con vida a todas las mujeres?
es.R: Moisés les dijo: «¿{{plural_you:Dejaron|Dejasteis}} vivir a todas las mujeres?

fr.L: Et Moïse leur dit : « Avez-vous laissé en vie toute femme ?
fr.B: Moïse leur dit : « Vous avez laissé la vie à toutes les femmes ?
fr.R: Moïse leur a dit : « Vous avez laissé vivre toutes les femmes ?

sw.L: Musa akawaambia, "Je, mmemwacha hai kila mwanamke?
sw.B: Musa akawaambia, "Mmewaacha hai wanawake wote?
sw.R: Musa akawaambia, "Mliwaacha wanawake wote waishi?

vi.L: Và Môi-se nói với họ: "Các ngươi đã để cho mọi người nữ sống sao?
vi.B: Môi-se nói với họ: "Anh em đã để cho tất cả phụ nữ sống sao?
vi.R: Môi-se nói với họ: "Anh em lại để cho tất cả phụ nữ sống sao?

ko.L: 그리고 모세가 그들에게 말했다. "너희가 모든 여자를 살려 두었느냐?
ko.B: 모세가 그들에게 말했다. "너희가 여자들을 모두 살려 두었단 말이냐?
ko.R: 모세가 그들에게 말했다. "너희가 여자들을 다 살려 두었느냐?

pt.L: E Moisés lhes disse: "Vocês deixaram viver toda fêmea?
pt.B: Moisés lhes disse: "Vocês deixaram todas as mulheres com vida?
pt.R: Moisés disse a eles: "Vocês deixaram todas as mulheres vivas?

decisions.choice: a question of rebuke: you have spared all the women!
decisions.reason: The question does not ask for information; it reproaches the officers for what they did. The next verse gives the reason.

decisions.choice: women
decisions.reason: "Every female" here means the grown women of verse 9, as verses 17-18 show. Balanced and Readable say "women"; Literal keeps "female".

decisions.choice: toute femme
decisions.reason: French "femelle" is used of animals and would be insulting of people; Literal says "femme" for the Hebrew "female".

decisions.choice: Moses rebukes the officers in 해라체 at every level, Readable included
decisions.reason: The officers are under his command and the question is a rebuke (meaning decision); 합쇼체 with "여러분", used at Readable when Moses addresses all Israel, would soften it. Balanced "단 말이냐" carries the rebuke.

source.text: הֵ֣ן הֵ֜נָּה הָי֨וּ לִבְנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בִּדְבַ֣ר בִּלְעָ֔ם לִמְסָר־מַ֥עַל בַּיהוָ֖ה עַל־דְּבַר־פְּע֑וֹר וַתְּהִ֥י הַמַּגֵּפָ֖ה בַּעֲדַ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, they were for [the] sons of Israel, by [the] word of Balaam, to commit unfaithfulness against Yahweh in [the] matter of Peor, and was the plague in [the] congregation of Yahweh.

en.L: Look, they were the ones who, by the word of Balaam, caused the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel to commit unfaithfulness against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the matter of Peor, and the plague came on the congregation of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: These are the very women who, on Balaam's advice, led the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to be unfaithful to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the affair of Peor, so that the plague struck the congregation of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Balaam told these women how to lead the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to turn against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at Peor. That is why the deadly sickness struck {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s people.

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, ellas fueron las que, por la palabra de Balaam, hicieron que los hijos de Israel cometieran una infidelidad contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} en el asunto de Peor, y hubo plaga en la comunidad {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Precisamente estas mujeres, por consejo de Balaam, llevaron a los israelitas a ser infieles {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} en el asunto de Peor, de modo que la plaga hirió a la comunidad {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Balaam les dijo a estas mujeres cómo hacer que los israelitas se volvieran contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} en Peor. Por eso la enfermedad mortal atacó al pueblo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Voici, ce sont elles qui, par la parole de Balaam, ont amené les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël à commettre une infidélité envers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dans l’affaire de Peor, et le fléau a été dans la communauté {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Ce sont justement ces femmes qui, sur le conseil de Balaam, ont entraîné les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} à être infidèles {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} dans l’affaire de Peor, si bien que le fléau a frappé la communauté {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: C’est Balaam qui a dit à ces femmes comment pousser les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} à se détourner {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} à Peor. C’est pour cela que la maladie mortelle a frappé le peuple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Tazama, hao ndio waliowafanya wana wa Israeli, kwa neno la Balaamu, kuvunja uaminifu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} katika jambo la Peori, na pigo likawa katika jumuiya ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Hawa ndio wale wanawake ambao, kwa shauri la Balaamu, waliwaongoza Waisraeli kukosa uaminifu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} katika tukio la Peori, hata pigo likaipiga jumuiya ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Balaamu aliwaambia wanawake hawa jinsi ya kuwafanya Waisraeli wamwache {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} huko Peori. Ndiyo sababu ugonjwa wa kuua uliwapiga watu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Kìa, chính họ là những người, theo lời của Ba-la-am, đã khiến con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên phạm tội bất trung với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} trong việc tại Phê-o, và tai vạ đã giáng trên hội chúng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Chính những phụ nữ này, theo lời khuyên của Ba-la-am, đã dẫn dụ dân Y-sơ-ra-ên bất trung với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} trong vụ Phê-o, khiến tai vạ giáng trên hội chúng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Ba-la-am đã chỉ cho những phụ nữ này cách dụ dỗ dân Y-sơ-ra-ên quay lưng lại với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} tại Phê-o. Vì thế mà bệnh dịch chết người đã giáng trên dân của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

ko.L: 보아라, 이 여자들이 발람의 말을 따라 이스라엘 자손이 브올의 일에서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 신의를 저버리게 하였고, 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 회중에 재앙이 있었다.
ko.B: 바로 이 여자들이 발람의 꾀를 따라 브올 사건 때 이스라엘 백성을 꾀어 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 신의를 저버리게 하였다. 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 회중에 재앙이 내렸다.
ko.R: 발람이 이 여자들에게, 이스라엘 사람들을 꾀어 브올에서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 배반하게 하는 방법을 가르쳐 주었다. 그 때문에 무서운 병이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 백성을 덮쳤다.

pt.L: Eis que elas foram para os filhos de Israel, pela palavra de Balaão, [ocasião] de cometer infidelidade contra {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} no caso de Peor, e houve a praga na comunidade {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.B: Foram justamente estas mulheres que, por conselho de Balaão, levaram os israelitas a ser infiéis {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} no caso de Peor, e por isso a praga atingiu a comunidade {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.R: Balaão ensinou a estas mulheres como levar os israelitas a se voltar contra {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} em Peor. Foi por isso que a doença mortal atingiu o povo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.

decisions.choice: by the word of Balaam: Balaam advised the Midianites how to lead Israel astray
decisions.reason: Chapter 25 tells of the women of Moab and Midian who drew Israel to the worship of Baal of Peor, but it does not mention Balaam. Only here is his part told: having failed to curse Israel, he gave the advice that brought them under the LORD's anger. Later Scripture remembers him for this (Revelation 2:14).

decisions.choice: commit unfaithfulness: break faith with the LORD
decisions.reason: The word is used of a betrayal of trust, of taking what belongs to God or turning from him to other gods (5:6, 12; Leviticus 5:15). At Peor Israel joined in the sacrifices to another god (25:2-3).

decisions.choice: the plague: the deadly sickness that killed 24,000 at Peor
decisions.reason: The plague of 25:8-9 stopped when Phinehas acted, after 24,000 had died.

decisions.choice: turn against / deadly sickness
decisions.reason: Readable puts the idea of unfaithfulness in plain words and says what the plague was. It makes the women the subject, as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: "phạm tội bất trung với" (L) / "bất trung với" (B)
decisions.reason: The verb means to break faith with the LORD; "bất trung" names the betrayal.

decisions.choice: "신의를 저버리다" (Literal, Balanced), "배반하다" (Readable) for "commit unfaithfulness"; "재앙" (Literal, Balanced), "무서운 병" (Readable) for the plague
decisions.reason: The verb is breaking faith with the LORD (meaning decision); "브올" is the place of chapter 25, and "재앙" is the plague that killed 24,000 there; Readable names it a deadly sickness, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: elas foram para os filhos de Israel ... [ocasião] de cometer infidelidade
alternatives: elas fizeram os filhos de Israel cometer infidelidade (L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says that the women "were to the sons of Israel" for unfaithfulness. Literal keeps the structure and brackets "ocasião" (occasion), which Portuguese needs to make sense of it; Balanced and Readable say what they did, as the English does.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֕ה הִרְג֥וּ כָל־זָכָ֖ר בַּטָּ֑ף וְכָל־אִשָּׁ֗ה יֹדַ֥עַת אִ֛ישׁ לְמִשְׁכַּ֥ב זָכָ֖ר הֲרֹֽגוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And now kill every male among the little ones, and every woman knowing a man by lying of a male, kill.

en.L: And now kill every male among the little ones, and every woman who has known a man by lying with a male, kill.
en.B: So now kill every boy among the children, and kill every woman who has slept with a man.
en.R: So now kill all the boys, and kill every woman who has had sexual relations with a man.

es.L: Y ahora, {{plural_you:maten|matad}} a todo varón entre los pequeños, y a toda mujer que haya conocido varón acostándose con él, {{plural_you:mátenla|matadla}}.
es.B: Así que ahora {{plural_you:maten|matad}} a todos los niños varones, y {{plural_you:maten|matad}} a toda mujer que se haya acostado con un hombre.
es.R: Así que ahora {{plural_you:maten|matad}} a todos los niños varones, y también a todas las mujeres que hayan tenido relaciones sexuales con un hombre.

fr.L: Et maintenant, tuez tout mâle parmi les petits enfants, et toute femme qui a connu un homme en partageant la couche d’un mâle, tuez-la.
fr.B: Maintenant donc, tuez tous les garçons parmi les enfants, et tuez toute femme qui a couché avec un homme.
fr.R: Alors maintenant, tuez tous les garçons, et tuez toutes les femmes qui ont eu des relations sexuelles avec un homme.

sw.L: Basi sasa, waueni wote wa kiume miongoni mwa watoto wadogo, na kila mwanamke aliyemjua mwanamume kwa kulala na mume, muueni.
sw.B: Basi sasa waueni wavulana wote miongoni mwa watoto, na muueni kila mwanamke aliyelala na mwanamume.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo sasa waueni wavulana wote, na waueni pia wanawake wote waliowahi kufanya tendo la ndoa na mwanamume.

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ, hãy giết mọi người nam trong đám trẻ con, và mọi người nữ đã biết người nam qua việc ăn nằm với người nam, hãy giết đi.
vi.B: Vậy bây giờ, hãy giết hết các bé trai, và giết mọi phụ nữ đã ăn nằm với đàn ông.
vi.R: Vậy bây giờ hãy giết hết các bé trai, và giết mọi phụ nữ đã từng có quan hệ với đàn ông.

ko.L: 그러니 이제 어린아이들 가운데 남자는 모두 죽이고, 남자와 동침하여 남자를 안 여자도 모두 죽여라.
ko.B: 그러니 이제 아이들 가운데 사내아이는 모두 죽이고, 남자와 잠자리를 같이한 여자도 모두 죽여라.
ko.R: 그러니 이제 사내아이들은 모두 죽여라. 남자와 잠자리를 같이한 여자도 모두 죽여라.

pt.L: E agora matem todo macho entre os pequeninos, e toda mulher que conheceu homem, deitando-se com macho, matem.
pt.B: Agora, matem todos os meninos e matem toda mulher que já dormiu com um homem.
pt.R: Agora matem todos os meninos e matem toda mulher que já teve relações sexuais com um homem.

decisions.choice: known a man by lying with a male: had sexual relations with a man
decisions.reason: "Know" is a common way of speaking of sexual union (Genesis 4:1), and "the lying of a male" makes it explicit. The order singles out the women who could have been among those who took part at Peor (verse 16).

decisions.choice: every male among the little ones: the boys
decisions.reason: With the men already dead (verse 7), the order ends the male line of these Midianite families. The command is part of the LORD's judgment on Midian for Peor (25:17-18; verses 2-3); the text reports it and does not explain it further.

decisions.choice: every boy among the children / all the boys
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "boy" for "male among the little ones", and give the idiom of sexual relations in plain words.

decisions.choice: "남자와 동침하여 남자를 안" (Literal), "남자와 잠자리를 같이한" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The idiom means having had sexual relations with a man (meaning decision); Literal keeps "know", Balanced and Readable use the plain, decent Korean expression.

source.text: וְכֹל֙ הַטַּ֣ף בַּנָּשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־יָדְע֖וּ מִשְׁכַּ֣ב זָכָ֑ר הַחֲי֖וּ לָכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And all the little ones among the women who have not known lying of a male, keep alive for yourselves.

en.L: But all the little ones among the women who have not known lying with a male, keep alive for yourselves.
en.B: But keep alive for yourselves all the girls who have not slept with a man.
en.R: But you may keep alive for yourselves all the girls who have never had sexual relations with a man.

es.L: Pero a todas las pequeñas de entre las mujeres que no han conocido acostarse con varón, {{plural_you:consérvenlas|conservadlas}} con vida para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:conserven|conservad}} con vida para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} a todas las muchachas que no se han acostado con un hombre.

decisions.choice: keep alive for yourselves: take into Israelite households
decisions.reason: The girls were to live among Israel as part of the households of their captors, as servants and in time as wives. Deuteronomy 21:10-14 gives the law for a man who wanted to marry a woman taken captive in war, and protects her from being sold or treated as a slave.

decisions.choice: the little ones among the women: the young girls
decisions.reason: The phrase is the counterpart of "every male among the little ones" (verse 17). Verse 35 counts them at 32,000.

decisions.choice: the girls
decisions.reason: As in verse 17, Balanced and Readable say "girls" for "the little ones among the women".

records.literal_gloss: And you, camp outside of the camp seven days; anyone killing a person and anyone touching [the] slain, purify yourselves on the day the third and on the day the seventh, you and your captives.

en.L: And you, camp outside the camp seven days; everyone who has killed a person and everyone who has touched [one] slain, purify yourselves on the third day and on the seventh day, you and your captives.
en.B: As for you, camp outside the camp for seven days. All of you who have killed anyone or touched anyone killed must purify yourselves and your captives on the third day and on the seventh day.
en.R: Any of you who killed someone or touched a dead body must stay outside the camp for seven days. You must purify yourselves and your captives on the third day and on the seventh day.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:acampen|acampad}} fuera del campamento siete días; todo el que haya matado a una persona y todo el que haya tocado [a un] muerto, {{plural_you:purifíquense|purificaos}} al tercer día y al séptimo día, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} cautivos.

es.R: Todos los que hayan matado a alguien o hayan tocado un cadáver {{plural_you:deben quedarse|debéis quedaros}} fuera del campamento siete días. {{plural_you:Tienen que purificarse|Tenéis que purificaros}}, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} cautivos, al tercer día y al séptimo día.

fr.L: Et vous, campez hors du camp sept jours ; quiconque a tué une personne et quiconque a touché [un] tué, purifiez-vous le troisième jour et le septième jour, vous et vos captifs.

fr.R: Tous ceux d’entre vous qui ont tué quelqu’un ou touché un cadavre doivent rester hors du camp pendant sept jours. Vous devez vous purifier, vous et vos captifs, le troisième jour et le septième jour.

sw.L: Nanyi, pigeni kambi nje ya kambi siku saba; kila aliyeua mtu na kila aliyegusa [mtu] aliyeuawa, jisafisheni siku ya tatu na siku ya saba, ninyi na mateka wenu.

vi.L: Còn các ngươi, hãy đóng trại bên ngoài trại quân bảy ngày; mọi người đã giết một người và mọi người đã chạm vào [người] bị giết, hãy tẩy sạch mình vào ngày thứ ba và vào ngày thứ bảy, các ngươi và các phu tù của các ngươi.

pt.L: E vocês, acampem fora do acampamento sete dias; todo aquele que matou uma pessoa e todo aquele que tocou [num] morto, purifiquem-se no terceiro dia e no sétimo dia, vocês e os seus cativos.

decisions.choice: purify yourselves on the third day and the seventh day: the rite of chapter 19
decisions.reason: Whoever touched a dead body was unclean for seven days and was to be purified with the water of cleansing on the third and seventh days (19:11-12, 16-19). The law applies to those killed in battle as much as to any other death.

decisions.choice: purify yourselves: be cleansed from the uncleanness of death
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the root for sin, in the sense of removing it, and is used for the cleansing of people and things (8:21; 19:12). It is a ritual washing, not a punishment.

decisions.choice: the people named first
decisions.reason: Readable puts the people concerned first, so that it is clear who must stay outside the camp.

decisions.choice: "정결하게 하다" for "purify"
decisions.reason: The term sheet word; the rite is the one of chapter 19 (meaning decision), cleansing from the uncleanness of death.

decisions.choice: purificar-se; puro (verse 24)
decisions.reason: "Purificar-se" is the Portuguese for the ritual cleansing from the uncleanness of death (m2), as Numbers 19 and the book's "puro/impuro" have it; it is not a washing for dirt, so "limpar-se" is not used.

decisions.choice: the statute of the law: a standing rule of the LORD's instruction
decisions.reason: The same phrase opens the law of the red heifer and the water of cleansing (19:2). Eleazar applies that law, and adds a rule for metals, which can go through fire.

decisions.choice: Eleazar speaks: the priest teaches the rules of clean and unclean
decisions.reason: The priests were to teach Israel the difference between clean and unclean (Leviticus 10:10-11). Moses gave the order in verses 19-20; the priest gives the details.

decisions.choice: rule
decisions.reason: Readable says "rule" for "statute" in this sentence, which joins it with "law".

decisions.choice: Eleazar to the soldiers: "các ngươi" (L), "anh em" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The priest speaks to Israel's men as Moses does, with the same forms.

decisions.choice: Eleazar speaks to the soldiers in 해라체 at every level
decisions.reason: The priest teaches the rules of clean and unclean to the men returning from battle (meaning decision); he speaks with the authority of the law, as Moses does to the officers in verse 15.

decisions.choice: lift up the head: take a count
decisions.reason: The phrase is the one used for the census (1:2; 26:2): to count people or things one by one.

decisions.choice: the heads of the fathers: the heads of the ancestral families
decisions.reason: These are the leaders of the family groups within the tribes (1:4). They share in the count so that the division is seen to be fair.

decisions.choice: take the count
decisions.reason: Literal gives the sense of the idiom, which would mislead word for word.

decisions.choice: Junto con Eleazar ..., cuenta
alternatives: Tú, Eleazar ... y los jefes ... harán el recuento
decisions.reason: The Hebrew command is addressed to Moses alone, with the others named after it; putting them first with "junto con" keeps the singular "cuenta" instead of a plural verb that would need a plural_you form.

decisions.choice: "머릿수를 세다" for "lift up the head"
decisions.reason: As Korean Numbers 1:2: the idiom means to take a count (meaning decision), and "머릿수" keeps the word "head".

decisions.choice: Faze o levantamento (L)
decisions.reason: The English Literal gives the sense of the census idiom here, "take the count". Portuguese "fazer o levantamento", the ordinary phrase for taking a count, keeps the verb "levantar" of the idiom (m1), as Numbers 1:2 keeps it with "levantem a cabeça"; "levantar a cabeça da presa" would read as lifting an animal's head. Verse 49 says the same.
